To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Mathematician Ridge (MR) is a seafloor ridge that is part of the Clipperton Ridge (CR), which is a seafloormid-ocean ridge system.

1) Mathematician Ridge, a north-south striking mid-oceanic ridge in the eastern Pacific Ocean, is the site of seafloor spreading and the generation of new crust at the equator; 2) the spreading rate is 2.5 cm/year, and the ridge is about 3.5 million years old; 3) the ridge is a continuation of the East Pacific Rise, which is a major spreading center in the equatorial Pacific; and 4)
Mathematician Ridge is a seafloor-spreading center that is currently inactive and that it is a remnant of the older Clipperton Ridge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the topographic and bathymetric features of the Clipperton Ridge and Mathematician Ridge (Fig. 2).
an attempt to apply the depth–age correlation to the East Pacific Rise south of 20° S, and to the Clipperton Ridge system.
the application of a new technique for age determination of oceanic crust to an area of the Pacific where the crust is not generated by a seamount chain, but by a mid-ocean ridge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the East Pacific Rise system is a seafloor-spreading system which has generated new ocean floor at a constant rate of about 5 cm yr−1 since 5 Ma ago.
the age-depth correlation is valid for the East Pacific Rise, but only for the portion between 0° N and 20° N, and between 0 and 20°S.
the crust of the East Pacific Rise between 20° S and the equator was generated at a constant rate of 2.2 cm a–1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the crust is about 1.5 m.y. old at the equator and increases in age northwards and southwards at a rate of about 1 km per million years, with the crust about 3 m.y. old in the vicinity of 20° N or S. This
the East Pacific Rise is a continuous system of crust formation from 20° S to the equator and from the equator to the Gulf of California.
the age of the crust generated by the equatorial East Pacific Rise system is less than 1 million years.

the ridge is a topographic high and not a magnetic anomaly, so the age dating is not reliable.
